answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable stake rather than a free signup. Think of reputation as an orchard: it takes time and real work to grow, so spawning thousands of fake trees yields nothing overnight. Every new agent enters through a single audited inlet where it must anchor its identity to a unique device attestation plus a small refundable bond that is slashed on fraud. Cheap clones cannot pass that gate at scale, while honest agents keep their bond and harvest trust over time.
